A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spherical Steering research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and page-layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, activation analyses, ablations, and generated examples, including additional LLaMA-3.1-8B experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds contrastive-data sensitivity experiments and generation-throughput measurements in Tables 4 and 6.

M1.justification: Contrastive prototype construction, norm-preserving spherical interpolation, vMF gating, and token-wise inference remain unchanged. Explicit layer indices and the antipodal caveat refine the description without documenting a new intervention procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six benchmarks and retain TruthfulQA multiple-choice and free-generation tasks. The new studies vary contrastive sample counts and measure runtime; they introduce no new dataset, population, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched evaluations retain ITI, CAA, SADI-HEAD, unsteered controls, and the relevant ICL comparisons. The new runtime experiment reuses CAA, SADI-HEAD, and an unsteered control; no new comparison algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: New auxiliary protocols reserve 408 TruthfulQA questions for testing while varying prototype-training counts from 25 to 409, and measure generation throughput with batch size 1, 128 tokens per prompt, and shared instrumentation. Existing benchmark splits and evaluation metrics in Appendix C remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds systematic sensitivity analysis of contrastive-data quantity and random selection across both instruction-tuned models. Section 6 adds comparative runtime profiling. These introduce substantive evidence about data dependence and computational cost beyond the retained gating, layer, ICL, strength, and representation analyses.

E5.justification: V2 introduces performance means and standard deviations over 10 random seeds for each sample count from 25 through 300, explicitly distinguishing the single-run 409-question setting. Runtime measurements average 50 timed runs and include ± values, whose statistic is not explicitly defined. This substantially extends uncertainty reporting beyond v1's activation-norm spread; main benchmark tables remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Two new result sets establish data-sensitivity and runtime findings. Table 4 reports LLaMA MC1 of 51.52±2.24 with 25 training questions and 53.92±0.35 with 300. Table 6 reports Spherical Steering overhead of 2.25%/1.78% on LLaMA/Qwen, versus 9.09%/8.31% for SADI-HEAD. These are additional experimental results; existing benchmark, ablation, figure, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 10's stated domain changes from theta not equal to zero to 0 < theta < pi. V2 explains that antipodal endpoints have nonunique shortest geodesics and constitute a degenerate case. This corrects a mathematical boundary condition; Appendix A's derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free activation rotation with confidence gating, improved accuracy–generation trade-offs, and greater collapse-efficiency. Abstract and contribution wording is edited, but the principal scientific claims and conclusion retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces the inference that behavioral information must reside in direction with the qualified interpretation that magnitude is a weak discriminator in this setting and direction may carry more information. V2 also interprets the new studies as evidence of prototype stabilization, effectiveness with few examples, and lightweight computation.

D1.justification: The runtime study newly specifies an A100-40GB GPU, BF16, HuggingFace Transformers, torch.inference_mode(), and shared baukit TraceDict hooks. These document the new experiment. Existing hyperparameter guidance, dataset preparation, prompts, judge-model references, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Agarwal et al. (2025), the gpt-oss model card, to the introduction and bibliography. No corresponding gpt-oss evaluation is reported. The related-work discussion and distinctions from Angular Steering and Householder pseudo-rotation remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized edits to the abstract, introduction, method notation, and analysis prose. It inserts a data-sensitivity subsection, a runtime section, and acknowledgements while retaining the overall narrative and appendix organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds sensitivity Table 4 and runtime Table 6, renumbers the retained strength-sweep and appendix tables, and adjusts page breaks and float placement. All six original figures retain their content. The document's visual design remains broadly unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence for robustness to contrastive-data selection and low runtime overhead, with explicit repeated-run reporting for the added experiments. Correcting the interpolation domain and qualifying the activation-norm interpretation improve precision. The overall gain is limited because the principal experimental findings are retained and uncertainty reporting still does not extend to the main benchmark comparisons.
